summary.title: DelTA: Discriminative Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards

setting_and_object.category: Algorithm (with an accompanying analytical view of RLVR updates)

details: RLVR gives one scalar advantage per response yet updates are accumulated token-by-token, so which token probabilities rise or fall is decided implicitly.

Analytical view: a first-order sequence-level RLVR update acts as a linear discriminator over token-gradient vectors, whose positive/negative reference directions are the advantage-weighted centroids of token gradients on each side; these centroids are pulled toward shared high-frequency directions (e.g. formatting tokens), so a good within-side summary is a poor between-side discriminator.

DelTA: a token credit-assignment method that reweights each token's term in a clipped, self-normalized RLVR surrogate by a stop-gradient coefficient measuring how much more that token's gradient vector resembles its own advantage-side centroid than the opposite side's.

Coefficients come from an entropy-regularized soft assignment (closed form: sigmoid of the squared-distance margin between the two centroids divided by an adaptive temperature), with a few alternating refinement steps that recompute each side's centroid as a score-weighted average, then a linear map to a bounded range [λmin, λmax].

Effect: amplifies side-specific token-gradient directions and downweights shared/weakly discriminative ones, thereby making the induced discriminator's reference directions more contrastive and reshaping the update direction.
Backbones: Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen3-14B-Base (plus Olmo3-7B-Base for generality); trained with VeRL on DeepMath-103K with binary answer-correctness reward (math-verify).
DAPO-style surrogate: clip low/high 0.2/0.28, KL coefficient 0, batch 128, 16 rollouts per prompt, max response 20,480 tokens, LR 1e-6; dynamic sampling disabled for all methods.
DelTA settings: [λmin, λmax] = [0.8, 1.2], K = 1 refinement iteration; coefficients computed once per rollout batch and fixed across optimization epochs.
Token gradients approximated by a layer-restricted LM-head proxy (1 - p_t(y_t))·h_t instead of full-parameter gradients; adds K+2 extra actor forward passes.

Seven math competition benchmarks (AIME24/25/26, HMMT25 Feb & Nov, HMMT26 Feb, Brumo25), 16 samples per problem, max 30,000 generation tokens; checkpoint chosen by best AIME25 avg@8 under the same rule for all methods.
Additional: code generation (HumanEval+, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench, trained on Eurus2-RL-Code) and OOD evaluation (GPQA-Diamond, 600-question MMLU-Pro subset).
DAPO (main baseline), DAPO with forking (top-20% high-entropy) tokens, SAPO (soft clipping gate), FIPO (Future-KL influence reweighting); all trained with identical shared hyperparameters.
Appendix casts GRPO/DAPO/forking-tokens/FIPO as different effective per-token weights in the same centroid-estimation framework.
Within-side-only coefficient variant (drops opposite-side distance); random-λ baseline; alternative top-K hidden-gradient proxy.
Component ablations: no adaptive temperature, no entropy regularizer (hard 0/1), no coefficient-mass normalizer, no range map, no centroid refinement.
Hard token-selection probe: train DAPO on the top / random / bottom 50% of tokens ranked by λ.
Hyperparameter sweeps over λ range and K∈{1,2,3}; evaluation-run-level one-sided Mann-Whitney U significance test over 16 evaluation repetitions.

key_findings.finding: DelTA consistently and substantially outperforms strong sequence-level RLVR baselines on mathematical reasoning at two model scales.
key_findings.evidence: Average over seven math benchmarks rises from 25.14 (best same-scale baseline, SAPO) to 28.40 on Qwen3-8B-Base and from 37.29 (FIPO) to 39.91 on Qwen3-14B-Base, with the best score on every individual benchmark; gains are significant under a one-sided Mann-Whitney U test over 16 evaluation repetitions.

key_findings.finding: The learned coefficients identify tokens whose gradient directions carry the learning signal, and low-coefficient tokens actively harm the update rather than merely being uninformative.
key_findings.evidence: Training standard DAPO on only the top-50% λ tokens beats full-token DAPO in both training reward and evaluation accuracy, random 50% selection tracks DAPO, and bottom-50% training collapses.

key_findings.finding: The opposite-side (between-side) contrast, not own-side centrality, is what makes the reweighting work.
key_findings.evidence: A within-side-only variant using only distance to its own centroid scores 17.94 average on four math benchmarks, below both DelTA (23.27) and DAPO (19.05).

key_findings.finding: Every design component contributes, with the centroid refinement iteration mattering most, while gains are not attributable to arbitrary reweighting or to the specific gradient proxy.
key_findings.evidence: Ablation averages drop from 23.27 to 19.97 without refinement, 20.78 without the bounded range map, 20.93 with hard assignment, 21.19 without adaptive temperature, 21.39 without coefficient-mass normalization; random λ in the same range gives 18.34, whereas an alternative top-K hidden-gradient proxy improves to 24.29; K=2/3 refinement degrades to ~22.2.
